relationships.note: The Air Quality Scrutiny Panel is described in the corpus as an Ealing Council scrutiny panel.
The cited reporting records Southall Waterside remediation and odour as evidence considered at the panel's September 2018 meeting.
The cited reporting identifies Berkeley Group as the developer of the former Southall Gasworks site, branded Southall Waterside and later The Green Quarter.
The cited reporting explicitly describes Blair Peach Primary School as adjacent to Southall Waterside / the former gasworks site.
The cited reporting records Leydon answering questions at the panel's September 2018 meeting.
The cited reporting identifies Berkeley Group as Damian Leydon's employer and describes him as Operations Director at Southall Waterside.
The cited reporting identifies Dr John Freeman as a Regulatory Services Officer at Ealing Council.
Ealing Council identifies itself as the local planning authority responsible for overseeing regeneration and contaminated-land treatment requirements at the site.

Ealing Council's end-of-term progress report records that in June 2025 the council purchased 180 homes from Berkeley Group at the Green Quarter for affordable housing, including 96 social-rent and 84 London Living Rent homes.
Official Ealing Council records list Berkeley Homes among sponsors of the council's MIPIM delegation. This records sponsorship, not any inferred effect on planning decisions.
Ealing Council's published roles page identifies the Environment Agency as the regulator for land remediation and soil treatment at the site.
The cited post identifies Henry Construction as the builder contracted on the Norwood Road housing scheme.
The cited reporting and linked SCA governance page identify Jags Sanghera as chair.
The cited reporting records Sanghera's Berkeley role and career history.
The cited reporting identifies Julian Bell as Ealing Council leader at the time.
The cited reporting records Bell's MIPIM attendance through Ealing's developer-sponsored delegation; official council records list Berkeley Homes among the sponsors.
Peter Mason is described in the cited reporting as council leader.
The cited reporting records that Mason's 2019 MIPIM attendance was jointly funded by a sponsor consortium that included Berkeley Group; Mason later described accepting the sponsorship as a mistake.
PHE reviewed air-monitoring data and provided public-health advice for the Southall Waterside development.
The cited post identifies the Southall Air Quality Focus Area as a defined area within Southall.
The cited reporting states that Southall Community Alliance has a presence on the Southall Town Team.
The cited reporting describes the Town Team as a council-facilitated body.
The cited post identifies Tony Pidgley as founder and chair of Berkeley Group.
